input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM ROCm functional and performance parity

## Description

This epic resolves the platform's lack of first-hand ROCm data by running a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct accelerators. It produces functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set (ROCm vs. the shipped CUDA builds) and a go/no-go recommendation that defines the scope of vLLM ROCm runtime productization. The campaign also performs first-time environment bring-up of the AMD software stack (ROCm driver/runtime, GPU device plugin exposing `amd.com/gpu`) on OpenShift, since no AMD hardware exists in the CI fleet today.

## Scope

- Bring up the AMD software stack (ROCm driver and runtime, GPU device plugin / GPU operator exposing `amd.com/gpu` resources) on the AMD Instinct nodes and target OpenShift version.
- Drive resolution of hardware access (procurement or partner-lab engagement) — the open access path is tracked here as scope and risk; access being granted is externally controlled and is not an acceptance criterion.
- For each model in the supported model set, run vLLM ROCm serving and collect:
  - functional correctness results (does the model serve correctly on ROCm),
  - performance parity data against the shipped CUDA builds of the same runtime (throughput, latency).
- Compile results into a validation report stating, per model, whether ROCm serving meets the functional and performance bar, and a go/no-go recommendation with the proposed productization scope.
- Track alignment (or misalignment) of upstream vLLM ROCm image releases with our release trains and record the findings in the report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The AMD software stack is running on the AMD Instinct environment and `amd.com/gpu` resources are discoverable by workloads on the target OpenShift version.
- A validation report exists covering every model in the supported model set, with per-model functional correctness results and performance measurements against the CUDA baseline.
- The report states a go/no-go recommendation and an explicit list of models cleared for productization.
- Upstream ROCm image cadence observations relevant to release-train alignment are recorded in the report.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks and Notes

- Hardware access is unresolved: dedicated AMD Instinct nodes require procurement or partner-lab access. The campaign's start and duration are exposed to externally controlled procurement and lab schedules; securing access is part of this epic's work, but access being granted is not a condition this epic's deliverable can produce.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities and may not align with our release trains.
- Performance parity thresholds for the go/no-go call involve product judgment; the epic produces the data and a recommendation, and the productization decision is confirmed with product stakeholders.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for campaign-cleared models

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by the AMD Instinct validation campaign. It turns the validated ROCm builds into a productized runtime image and serving runtime definition that ships alongside the existing CUDA builds, so RHOAI can serve the cleared model set on AMD Instinct accelerators under KServe InferenceServices.

## Scope

- Build and release the vLLM ROCm runtime image in the existing vLLM midstream build and release pipeline, for the model set cleared by the validation campaign.
- Define/extend the serving runtime definition (ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime) for the ROCm vLLM image, requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources, alongside the existing CUDA variants.
- Ensure the runtime's release alignment with the platform release train, using the upstream ROCm image cadence findings from the validation campaign.
- Declare the support scope (supported models, driver prerequisites) for the productized runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A productized vLLM ROCm runtime image is built and released through the platform's build pipeline with a green pipeline run.
- A serving runtime definition exists that deploys the ROCm vLLM image, and the runtime successfully serves each campaign-cleared model under KServe InferenceServices on AMD GPU nodes (serverless and/or raw deployment mode as supported).
- The runtime image and definition are included in a platform release, with the supported model list and driver prerequisites stated.
- The support scope matches the go/no-go list from the validation campaign — no model is declared supported without campaign clearance.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks and Notes

- Scope is gated by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome: productize only the cleared subset; if no model achieves parity, this epic is dropped and the campaign results feed a follow-up strategy.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and may affect release-train alignment; misalignment is a timing risk, not a scope change.
- This runtime is additive alongside the existing CUDA builds — it does not replace an existing capability, so no rollback/feature-flag path is required beyond standard release practices.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) for jobs managed by the Training Operator: single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorchJob runs using ROCm-enabled PyTorch images, admitted through Kueue like their CUDA counterparts. It delivers the training-side enablement of the strategy independently of the serving validation campaign, since training can proceed on currently published upstream ROCm PyTorch images.

## Scope

- Validate and enable PyTorchJob execution on ROCm GPU nodes for single- and multi-GPU job topologies, using ROCm-enabled PyTorch training images.
- Address any Training Operator changes needed for ROCm jobs (resource requests for `amd.com/gpu`, container/env requirements of the ROCm runtime) identified during enablement.
- Document/validate the recommended ROCm PyTorch training image usage for PyTorchJob specs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm-enabled PyTorch image runs to completion on AMD GPU nodes and is admitted through Kueue.
- A multi-GPU (and multi-node, where the topology applies) PyTorchJob using a ROCm-enabled PyTorch image runs to completion on AMD GPU nodes and is admitted through Kueue with gang semantics.
- Job specs requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources are handled correctly by the Training Operator (scheduling and completion).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. (This epic covers the job-execution half; Kueue quota handling is covered separately.)

## Risks and Notes

- Assumes `amd.com/gpu` resources are exposed on nodes via the AMD GPU Operator / ROCm driver stack; environment bring-up is validated by the serving-side validation campaign and is cluster-infrastructure work outside this epic.
- Functional validation of training on ROCm requires access to AMD Instinct hardware (same availability risk as the validation campaign).
- Upstream ROCm PyTorch image cadence is controlled by AMD and the PyTorch community.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm workloads

## Description

This epic ensures the Distributed Workloads queueing layer (Kueue) handles `amd.com/gpu` resource quota correctly, so ROCm training and serving workloads are admitted under the platform's quota model just like CUDA workloads. It covers quota configuration/coverage for the AMD resource name in the ClusterQueue/LocalQueue model and any Kueue changes the enablement surfaces.

## Scope

- Validate and enable `amd.com/gpu` quota handling in Kueue: ClusterQueue/LocalQueue resource flavors and quota accounting for the AMD GPU resource name.
- Address any Kueue changes needed for `amd.com/gpu` admission (resource flavor coverage, quota accounting) identified during enablement.
- Provide the recommended queue/quota configuration for AMD GPU workloads (to be reflected in user documentation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ClusterQueue/LocalQueue configuration admits workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources with correct quota accounting, including all-or-nothing (waitForPodsReady) admission semantics.
- Quota for `amd.com/gpu` is enforced: workloads exceeding the configured quota stay pending and are admitted when quota frees up.
- Kueue metrics (pending/admitted workloads per queue) correctly report AMD GPU workload admission.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. (This epic covers the quota-handling half; PyTorchJob execution is covered separately.)

## Risks and Notes

- Assumes `amd.com/gpu` resources are exposed on nodes via the AMD GPU Operator / ROCm driver stack; environment bring-up is validated by the serving-side validation campaign and is cluster-infrastructure work outside this epic.
- End-to-end validation (a PyTorchJob admitted with `amd.com/gpu` quota) is an acceptance criterion on the training-side epic; this epic's own deliverable is the quota handling layer.
- Functional validation on real AMD hardware requires the same hardware access as the validation campaign.

# Document supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and validated model list

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: what AMD hardware is supported, the driver and software prerequisites for serving and training on ROCm, and the list of models validated on the ROCm serving runtime. It documents the as-built state of the serving runtime productization, training support, and quota setup.

## Scope

- New documentation topics covering:
  - supported AMD Instinct hardware for RHOAI serving and training,
  - driver and software prerequisites (ROCm driver/runtime, GPU operator/device plugin, node requirements),
  - the validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, as cleared by the validation campaign,
  - how to run PyTorch training jobs on ROCm and configure `amd.com/gpu` quota in Kueue.
- Cross-references from existing serving and training documentation to the new AMD/ROCm topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list matching the productized runtime's support scope.
- Published documentation covers ROCm training job usage and `amd.com/gpu` quota configuration.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented serving runtime, training support, and quota handling (reviewed by the implementing engineers), with discrepancies resolved.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list.

## Risks and Notes

- Content is gated by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome (`gated_by` on this epic): the validated model list is a direct campaign deliverable, and on a no-go the productized-runtime sections fall away. On a no-go, this epic is rewritten to document the campaign outcome (parity findings, training/quota usage on AMD Instinct) with no validated model list; scheduling still waits for the productization, training, and quota work to complete.
- Priority derived from the strategy's overall priority (Major) per the docs-authoring exception, not from the HLR's P2 label.
